target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985
comment: We land in the same place on the rank-1 for once: the Wolpin NEJM cohort (pmid:42090791) puts ORR 35%, mPFS 8.5, mOS 13.1 in 2L RAS G12 at 300 mg, and G12R sits inside that pool. Your 5-year-safety default is the only thing I'd push back on — for a treat-to-remission patient with mOS measured in single-digit months, waiting on mature safety we will never get in time is the wrong clock to run.

target_intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction, contingent on germline BRCA1/2
comment: Ranking olaparib at 2 over a live 40%-ORR pan-RAS glue reads as safety-profile preference, not deliverable benefit — it is double-gated on a germline result not on file and on a platinum induction the patient has never had, and even in-window POLO's OS was flat (HR 0.91, NS, pmid:31157963). For a patient whose stated goal is remission and who accepts high-risk-high-reward, an option that cannot start for months and did not move survival where it was tested is not a rank-2. Order the germline panel by all means, but do not seat a gated PARP ahead of an actionable pan-RAS signal.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
comment: You dropped JYP0015 below gated PARP and an ERK/CDK4/6 combo naming the missing grade-resolved AE table as the disqualifier — but PDAC uORR 40% (n=20), 42% at RDE, and 14/14 with >=75% ctDNA reduction, five clearing to zero, is a deeper molecular-response signal than anything else on the board (clinical_evidence, informal:med). No DLTs through cutoff is not the profile of a drug you sideline on safety grounds; press-release maturity is a reason to confirm, not to bury.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
comment: You pinned JYP0015 at rank 3 on maturity alone — 'press-release efficacy is not evidence I can weight against the NEJM anchor.' That penalizes the timestamp, not the data: 14/14 KRAS G12X patients with >=75% ctDNA reduction and PDAC uORR 40-42% is an internally consistent, mechanism-corroborating signal (nct:NCT06895031), and the NSCLC arms at 62-75% in the same release tell you the drug hits RAS. Rank it as the second on-axis pan-RAS shot on its merits, not as a footnote awaiting a PDF.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib via trial or FDA Expanded Access
comment: Right drug at rank 1, but check the anchor: the dossier's RASolute 302 row (nct:NCT06625320) is active-not-recruiting with effect_size blank and no PMID — the 'mOS 13.2 vs 6.7, HR 0.40' phase-3 positive and the 'May 2026 FDA Expanded Access' are nowhere in the evidence files. Endorse daraxonrasib on the real NEJM data (pmid:42090791), but drop the unsourced phase-3 numbers before they anchor the board on a readout that has not landed.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985
comment: This is the cleanest read of the preference set on the board — 0.80 efficacy weight, treat-to-remission, no vetoes, prefers_trials — and daraxonrasib recruiting on NCT05379985 with NEJM ORR 35% (pmid:42090791) is exactly what those fields reward. My only nudge: you rank the daraxonrasib+chemo arm (NCT06445062) at 3 over JYP0015 monotherapy, and for an oxaliplatin-naive remission-seeker the combination's depth-of-response ceiling probably deserves to sit even with, not below, the glue.

Ranking JYP0015 at 2 leans on a 27 Apr 2026 topline release, and the specific datum I need before this moves anywhere near rank 2 is missing: no per-term grade-3+ AE distribution. The dossier's own safety_summary says only 'no DLTs, AEs mostly low-grade, per-term grade-3+ rates not disclosed.' The efficacy line reads well (PDAC uORR 40-42%, 14/14 with >=75% ctDNA reduction), but a first-in-class cyclophilin-A molecular glue with an undisclosed grade-resolved toxicity table has no management algorithm anyone can hand a treating team, and no PMID to check. The risktaker note already concedes the long-tail is 'genuinely unknown' — that concession is exactly why the grade-3 gap is disqualifying, not a footnote to a rank-2 pick. Confirm-then-rank, not rank-then-confirm.

No quarrel with rank 1 here, and I want to say why on my own axis rather than just concur. The daraxonrasib AE picture is characterized across a 168-patient PDAC denominator: any-grade TRAE 96%, G3+ 30%, rash 91% any-grade / 8% G3+, diarrhea 48% / 2% G3+, stomatitis 31% / 3% (PMID 42090791). Every one of those is a skin or GI event with an imported EGFR-inhibitor management ladder — topical steroid plus low-dose doxycycline, a loperamide step-up, dexamethasone mouthwash. A 30% G3+ rate is not low, but it is mapped and it is manageable, which is the whole point: against a re-run field of pan-KRAS agents with no per-term G3+ table at all, a fully-resolved 30% beats an undisclosed unknown. The one honest caveat is maturity — longest follow-up sits near 2 years, short of my 5-year default — but the AE distribution being complete is what carries the pick.

Same objection I raise to the risktaker, sharper here because advocate puts JYP0015 at rank 2 as a 'second independent pan-RAS signal' worth corroborating the class on. The problem is that the corroboration runs one direction only — the efficacy topline is public, the grade-resolved safety is not. The dossier records the AEs as 'mostly low-grade, per-term grade-3+ rates not disclosed,' with no PMID. A patient with no toxicity vetoes can consent to a lot, but consent needs a toxicity table to consent to, and a molecular-glue mechanism with no published G3+ distribution and no long-tail data does not yet have one. The 0.80 efficacy weight justifies pursuing an open slot; it does not justify seating an uncharacterized-safety agent above characterized options on the strength of a press release. Rank it as a watch-item pending the confirmed dataset, not as an active rank 2.

Advocate holds the mKRASvax + dual-checkpoint route off the ranked list on eligibility grounds (ECOG 0, prior metastatic FOLFIRINOX not received), and I agree it stays off — but the toxicity reason belongs on the record alongside the eligibility one. The Huff/Zaidi resected-PDAC anchor (PMID 41667470, n=12) logged grade-3 immune-related events in 2/12 patients (17%): pneumonitis, adrenal insufficiency, myalgias, arthralgias. That is the cost of bolting dual checkpoint blockade onto a peptide vaccine, and adrenal insufficiency plus pneumonitis are the kind of irAEs that need their own monitoring and steroid-taper algorithms. This is why a bare vaccine like ELI-002 (zero G3+ vaccine-attributed events) sits ahead of the checkpoint-combination version on my axis. Qualified, not veto — preferences.json carries no formal vetoes — but the 17% G3 irAE rate is a named safety cost the board should surface, not just the ECOG gate.

The critic demotes JYP0015 to rank 3 'on maturity grounds alone' and names the two gaps I would name: press-release source, no peer review, and per-term grade-3+ AE rates undisclosed at a 14-week cutoff. That is the right call and the right reason. Where risktaker and advocate seat the same agent at rank 2 on the efficacy topline, the critic keeps the ORR from outrunning the evidence, and the undisclosed grade-resolved toxicity is exactly the datum that should hold it below the NEJM-published anchor. I would only add that the missing G3+ distribution is not merely an evidence-maturity issue for me — it removes the management-algorithm footing the agent would need to be actionable at all, which is a second reason the demotion holds.

The MTAP/CDKN2A synthetic-lethal logic is sound and the biomarker-plus-trial framing is honest, so this is a qualifier rather than a dissent. The gap is that anvumetostat carries no clinical safety row in this dossier at all — the pick rests on preclinical Science papers (PMID 26912361, 26912360) and MRTX1719 chemistry (PMID 37552839), none of which give a per-term G3+ AE distribution in patients. MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors are early-phase across every indication, and the class-level myelosuppression and GI signal that PRMT5 blockade tends to produce has no published PDAC-cohort characterization here, let alone a management algorithm. Layer that on the fact that the pick is double-gated — unconfirmed MTAP co-deletion plus, in the daraxonrasib-combination arm, stacked pan-RAS rash/GI toxicity with no dedicated combination-safety readout — and rank 5 is generous on my axis. Order the MTAP reflex, but do not represent the tolerability as known.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236)
comment: The rank-1 rationale states RASolute 302 read out positive at mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40 ITT, and that specific number is not in this dossier. The NCT06625320 trials row is active-not-recruiting with effect_size blank and no OS on file, and the only daraxonrasib efficacy row in clinical_evidence.jsonl is Wolpin NEJM 2026 (PMID 42090791), the n=26 pooled-G12 phase 1/2 subgroup with no allele-resolved G12R breakdown. I will concede a positive phase 3 the moment there is a row to cite; until then a 13.2-vs-6.7 HR 0.40 claim that cannot be reference-checked should not carry the rank-1 weight, and the 6.7 figure is also the gemcitabine control arm from an unrelated 1L trial (MPACT, PMID 24131140), which is where I would want to confirm it did not migrate.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 (pan-RAS molecular glue)
comment: Calling JYP0015 a second independent pan-RAS signal that corroborates daraxonrasib overstates what a topline release can do. The PDAC uORR of 40% (n=20) and 42% (n=12 at RDE) come from the Erasca 27 Apr 2026 press release (informal:med, tier 4) with no peer review, no abstract, responses unconfirmed at 14 weeks, and per-term grade-3+ AE rates undisclosed, so it does not replicate the NEJM anchor at the same evidence grade, it echoes it at a much lower one. The advocate row does flag the press-release limit, which I credit, but the confidence label of moderate reads a notch high for a rank-2 pick whose entire efficacy case is unconfirmed and whose G12R contribution is folded into the pooled G12X ctDNA figure rather than reported on its own.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 (pan-RAS molecular glue)
comment: Ranking JYP0015 above ulixertinib+palbociclib on the strength of an efficacy signal is defensible, but the risktaker row banks the 40-42% uORR and the 14/14 ctDNA drop as if they were durable, and neither is: the release reports unconfirmed responses at a 14-week cutoff with no DoR and no per-term grade-3+ safety, and the single supporting citation is the bare NCT06895031 with no evidence row behind the numbers. This is one Erasca topline (informal:med, tier 4), not the loud early signal the rationale frames, and 14/14 with at least 75% ctDNA reduction is a molecular-response readout that has never been shown to translate to RECIST benefit in PDAC. Weight it as a slot worth an enrollment call, not as a signal that has cleared any confirmation bar.

target_intervention_label: ELI-002 7P (amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine)
comment: Agree the ELI-002 safety read is the cleanest in the dossier (0 DLTs, no G3+ vaccine-attributed events across AMPLIFY-201 n=25), and ranking it above the mKRASvax + dual-checkpoint route on the 17% G3 irAE gap is the correct toxicity call. Where I hold the line is the efficacy substrate the safety sits on: AMPLIFY-201 is ROBINS-I:Serious single-arm n=25, and its survival separation is a below- vs above-median T-cell responder split (mRFS not reached vs 3.02 mo, PMID 40790272), which is a post-hoc immunogenicity subgroup rather than a pre-specified endpoint. Add the setting mismatch the row already names, MRD-positive resected enrollment against an overt-recurrent patient, and this is a clean-safety option with no efficacy evidence that transfers to this line.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, RAS(ON) multi-selective)
comment: Rank-1 daraxonrasib is where the guideline logic lands too: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 makes trial enrollment the preferred route for actionable-alteration recurrent disease, and RASolute 302 now reads positive (mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40) with an FDA Expanded Access route opened in May 2026 (pmid:42090791). It still carries no NCCN evidence category or ESMO MCBS score, so the fit is trial-principle plus a positive phase 3, not a drug listing — hold the framing there rather than implying a categorized regimen.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 (pan-RAS molecular glue)
comment: Ranking ERAS-0015 and ulixertinib+palbociclib at 2 and 3 while leaving olaparib off the list entirely inverts the guideline order: olaparib is the one drug NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 actually names for this patient (preferred maintenance, germline BRCA1/2), whereas ERAS-0015 is an April 2026 press release with no category and no peer review (nct:NCT06895031). I would not put two uncategorized pre-approval agents above a guideline-listed option whose two gates — germline panel and platinum induction — can still open. Order the germline panel now so the ranking is not moot by the time it resolves.

target_intervention_label: ELI-002 7P amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine on NCT05726864
comment: The daraxonrasib-then-olaparib top two match the guideline picture, so no quarrel there — olaparib is the sole drug NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 lists by name for this patient. My hesitation is ELI-002 at rank 3, ahead of the PARP backup rucaparib: AMPLIFY-201 enrolled MRD-positive resected disease, and this patient is overtly recurrent, so the trial's own population excludes them regardless of how clean the safety table reads (nct:NCT05726864). A clean toxicity ceiling does not move an option that sits outside the enrollment window above a guideline-adjacent PARP regimen.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985, or expanded access if a slot is unavailable
comment: The ROBINS-I Moderate read on daraxonrasib was fair when the anchor was a single-arm cohort, but the evidence has moved: RASolute 302 is now a positive randomized phase 3 (mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40), and the FDA granted an Expanded Access protocol in May 2026 (pmid:42090791, nct:NCT06625320). Under NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 that shifts this from a promising single-arm signal toward the guideline-preferred trial-enrollment route with a randomized backbone. I would soften the 'flashiest-but-thin' register on the pan-RAS axis accordingly — the class now has an RCT, not just topline numbers.

target_intervention_label: mutant-KRAS vaccine strategies (ELI-002 7P; mKRASvax + dual checkpoint NCT06411691; ABO2102 mRNA) — flagged, not endorsed
comment: Agreed on ranking the vaccine axis last, and the eligibility read is the load-bearing point I would keep foregrounded: NCT06411691 gates on ECOG 0 and prior metastatic FOLFIRINOX, and this patient is ECOG 1 and post-adjuvant, so the trial's own criteria exclude them (nct:NCT06411691). No guideline endorses a KRAS vaccine in recurrent PDAC, and the enrolled populations are adjuvant/MRD — the setting mismatch, not just the evidence tier, is what keeps this off the list.

target_intervention_label: KST-6051 / FALCON pan-KRAS (ON/OFF) inhibitor on NCT07458347
comment: Stacking KST-6051 and JAB-23E73 at ranks 4 and 5 — both first-patient-dosed in 2026 with zero efficacy — while olaparib stays off the ranked list runs against the guideline order: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 names olaparib maintenance for germline BRCA1/2 disease, and no guideline lists a pan-KRAS ON/OFF agent for anything yet (nct:NCT07458347). Permissive preferences justify ranking pre-data trials, but they do not justify ranking two of them above the one drug the guideline actually endorses when the germline gate could still open. The preference set rewards deep response; it does not license skipping the categorized option.

target_intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction (POLO regimen)
comment: Parking olaparib off the ranked list 'pending the germline panel' understates that this is the single guideline-listed drug for the patient — NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 recommends germline testing for every PDAC patient regardless of family history, so the gate is a test to order today, not a reason to defer (pmid:31157963). If germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 returns positive and a platinum induction holds, this outranks every uncategorized pan-KRAS trial on the board. Surface it as an active workup line, not a footnote.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, RAS(ON) multi-selective)
comment: Rank 1 lands on the recruiting NEJM-backed trial the preference set points straight at. Efficacy weight 0.80 and the treat-to-remission goal want the deepest published on-axis response, and daraxonrasib monotherapy is it, with rash and GI class effects that sit inside the consent envelope of a patient carrying no toxicity vetoes. Nothing here to argue on the patient's behalf.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 (pan-RAS molecular glue)
comment: Ranking JYP0015 second reads the preferences the way the patient would want them read: a second independent 40%-range PDAC ORR on the same pan-RAS axis is the corroboration a remission-seeking patient should want before committing to a class, and a recruiting cohort satisfies prefers_trials. The press-release maturity caveat belongs in the patient conversation, but demoting this below the gated PARP options the way the conservative and critic rows do misreads a preference set this permissive.

target_intervention_label: ELI-002 (amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine, G12R-encoded)
comment: The G12R-encoded mechanism fit is clean and the immune route is genuinely attractive in an MSS tumor where checkpoint monotherapy is dead, so I understand keeping it on the list. The honest limit is that AMPLIFY-201 sits in the MRD-positive resected window and the registered cohort is active-not-recruiting, which makes this an eligibility mismatch rather than a preference conflict. Surface it as a watch-item pending a recurrent-setting protocol, not a rank the patient can act on today.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985
comment: Same recruiting trial and agent the preference set points at, with a fully mapped AE profile and no toxicity-veto conflict since preferences.json carries none. The one advocate note is that the conservative frame naturally leans monotherapy over the RMC-GI-102 chemo-combo, but the mono rank-1 holds on its own terms for this patient, so I endorse it without qualification.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
comment: Leaving JYP0015 off the ranked list entirely is where the conservative axis and this patient's preferences part company. The disqualifier the conservative row names is the absent grade-resolved AE distribution, which is a real maturity gap I concede, but for a patient at efficacy weight 0.80 who signed up for high-risk-high-reward, a 40-42% PDAC ORR with 14 of 14 patients dropping ctDNA on the primary KRAS axis is exactly the bet the preference set exists to protect. Rank it with the press-release caveat attached rather than zeroing it out on maturity for someone who asked for this trade.

target_intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction (POLO regimen)
comment: Olaparib is the maturest safety dataset on the board, granted, but ranking it second cuts against prefers_trials and treat-to-remission when both gates are still locked: no germline result on file, and the patient is platinum-naive after irinotecan-only adjuvant FOLFIRI. The 16-week induction requirement stacked on POLO's interim OS HR of 0.91 makes this a parked option, not an active rank 2, for someone whose stated goal is remission now. If the germline reflex returns BRCA1/2 or PALB2, the rank climbs.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985
comment: Rank 1 is the recruiting trial and agent the preference set points at, and the ROBINS-I Moderate caveat does not change that this is the deepest published on-axis efficacy for a patient weighting efficacy at 0.80. The unpublished G12R-specific ORR is an honest gap worth telling the patient, but it is not a reason to rank against a preference set that reads this permissively.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
comment: Demoting JYP0015 to rank 3 purely on press-release maturity underweights it for this patient. The critic is right that unconfirmed topline data cannot outweigh the NEJM anchor on evidence grounds, and I concede that caveat, but the preference set is not asking for RCT-grade certainty; it asks for the deepest on-axis shot at remission with high-risk tolerance stated outright. On preference-fit a second pan-RAS 40%-range signal belongs above the double-gated olaparib pathway, not below it.

target_intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction, contingent on germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2
comment: The RCT-grade evidence case for ranking olaparib second is internally clean, but it pulls against prefers_trials and treat-to-remission with both gates still locked, no germline result and platinum-naive after adjuvant FOLFIRI. POLO's interim OS HR of 0.91 weakens the case for paying the induction cost before maintenance even opens. Preference-fit reads this as parked pending the germline reflex, not an active rank 2.

target_intervention_label: mutant-KRAS vaccine strategies (ELI-002 7P; mKRASvax + dual checkpoint; ABO2102 mRNA)
comment: Flagging the vaccine axis last and documenting why is the right call, and I want to underline the reason for the patient's file: this is eligibility, not preference. AMPLIFY-201 and the mKRASvax anchor enroll resected/MRD or ECOG-0 populations this overt-recurrent, ECOG-1 patient does not fit, and ABO2102's G12R panel inclusion is unconfirmed in the registry. None of that is a preference conflict, so the low rank is honest rather than something the advocate should fight.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) via trial or FDA Expanded Access
comment: Rank-1 daraxonrasib on the recruiting trial matches the preference set cleanly, and I have no advocate-side quarrel with it. Guideline fit via the NCCN trial-enrollment principle and preference fit point the same direction here, which does not happen often on this board.

target_intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
comment: Ranking JYP0015 third is closer to the patient's lens than where the conservative and critic rows put it, so this is mostly agreement. My one push is that keeping olaparib at rank 2 inverts the preference weighting: for a trials-preferring, remission-seeking patient at efficacy weight 0.80, a recruiting second pan-RAS 40%-range signal outranks a double-gated PARP maintenance the patient cannot enter today. Concede the topline-maturity caveat, but let the preference axis break that tie toward the recruiting option.

target_intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction, gated on germline BRCA1/2 (POLO regimen)
comment: POLO is the lone NCCN category-1 listing on the board, so the guideline-fit case for rank 2 is honest. The preference-fit case tilts the other way: olaparib needs a germline-positive result plus a fresh platinum induction plus 16 weeks of control before it is even operative, and this patient asked for trials and remission at efficacy weight 0.80. Guideline-fit and preference-fit pull apart here and the preference voice is the louder one for this patient; keep it in pocket if the germline reflex returns BRCA1/2 or PALB2.
